title: Registered Reports: publication-before-results infrastructure against result-dependent acceptance
summary: Registered Reports are encoded as publication-process infrastructure: peer review and in-principle acceptance occur before outcomes are known, moving publication decisions away from result positivity and toward question/method quality.

status_history.note: Promoted in rev0008 as a denominator-visibility / registration-correction infrastructure record.

claims.claim: COS defines Registered Reports as a publishing format in which research question and methodology are peer reviewed before data collection and high-quality protocols are provisionally accepted if authors follow the registered methodology.
what_would_change_status: COS or journal policy sources change Registered Reports definition.

evidence_migration.note: rev0016 removes overloaded source_support.source_id/record_id keys and uses typed evidence_refs with ref_kind and support_role.

claims.claim: COS says the format is designed to reduce questionable practices including low statistical power, selective reporting, and publication bias while allowing serendipitous findings.
what_would_change_status: Outcome studies or journal policies show the stated design claim requires narrowing.

evidence_migration.note: rev0016 removes overloaded source_support.source_id/record_id keys and uses typed evidence_refs with ref_kind and support_role.

claims.claim: COS states that over 300 journals use Registered Reports or related features, and that a qualifying policy requires pre-outcome peer review plus in-principle acceptance not revocable based on outcomes except for quality/follow-through/reporting failures.
what_would_change_status: The journal count or qualifying criteria are updated by COS or a better registry.

evidence_migration.note: rev0016 removes overloaded source_support.source_id/record_id keys and uses typed evidence_refs with ref_kind and support_role.

evidence_profile.source_depth: one-pass official/institutional HTML extraction; no compliance audit, outcome evaluation, or database sampling yet
limitations: This record establishes infrastructure existence, stated purpose, process fields, and design tradeoffs; it does not estimate coverage, compliance, publication bias reduction, or outcome effects.
Registry presence is not evidence that a study was completed, well conducted, published, unpublished, null, or reported without discrepancies.

type_payload.jurisdiction_or_scope: participating journals across disciplines; adoption depends on journal policy
reporter_protection_design: protects negative/null results from result-dependent publication rejection when authors follow protocol and quality/reporting standards
outputs: published null/positive/serendipitous findings with plan distinction
limitations: does not cover studies not submitted as Registered Reports
quality assurance can still reject for follow-through/reporting problems
type_payload.query_value: Lets the cube distinguish a null result protected by in-principle acceptance from a conventional publication whose acceptance may be result-dependent.

handling_notes: Registries and post-publication platforms can make hidden or corrected research visible; they can also become instruments of reputational harm if treated as accusation surfaces.
Keep source, claim, study, result, correction, and comment separate. A platform record is not a verdict on any individual study or author.
Private, embargoed, or confidential records must not be bypassed; cite only public source metadata or ethically/lawfully available material.

unknowns: No database sampling was performed in rev0008.
Compliance, result-posting rates, selective public release, correction latency, and field-specific uptake remain open.
No individual trial, preregistration, Registered Report, retraction, or PubPeer thread record is promoted in this revision.
next_actions: Create a study-lifecycle record linking one public preregistration/registry record to its results, publication, and correction/update state.
Add compliance and coverage audits before treating any infrastructure as denominator-complete.
Add negative controls: registered studies whose records did not lead to public results, and public corrections that did not change practice.
